This is one of my areas of expertise.

The legal status of "employee" is part master servant law, and part contractual relationship law. It is a special legal status under which you have binding legal duties and obligations to the employer, and the employer has binding legal duties and obligations to you.

Basically, failure to keep you on and paid is the same as being fired under employment law. You are either working and being paid or you are not. If you are not then you no longer have a contractual work relationship with your employer. They can keep you at home, but they still have to pay you at your full wages to keep the contract in effect. If they are letting you go, they have to pay you whatever severance is required under the law.

A union contract replaces the implied default legal employment contract with a specific contract of employment, containing different terms and conditions. A union contract cannot contain terms and conditions that fail to meet the minimum implied standards contained in the default contract which is established by the legal jurisdiction. You cannot, for example, have a clause that pays less than minimum wage, or one that provides less holidays than the statutory requirement, without meeting the state schedule for wage compensation.

Layoffs also have special meaning under the law. It means you were not terminated for cause, but are temporarily released with the intention of fully reinstating your employment when business conditions are restored. In many government insurance programs, the status of laid off means you are not penalized for having been fired, and you might not be required to search for new work in order to maintain your benefits, because you are not actually fully unemployed yet. Your contract is suspended for a sometimes undetermined period, but not fully cancelled.
